messages:
anya: Quick follow-up on the offline packaging RFC — focusing on delivery and operator rollback playbook. TL;DR: we want a simple, auditable two-phase apply (stage -> activate) with an atomic switch and a compact rollback plan operators can run from an operator console. Questions below.

mira: +1 on two-phase. Can we keep the staged payload immutable and signed so operator only stores small manifest metadata? That keeps operator memory low. :thumbsup:

shankar: Yup, signatures must be verified before stage. Recommend a short signature chain: manifest -> blob list -> sig. Keep verification incremental so you can stream-verify without storing whole blob.

leo: Edge case: powercut during activation. If swap is a simple rename it’s atomic, but partial filesystem operations (overlay mounts, services) can leave node inconsistent. We should record a single activation.marker and ensure systemd unit dependencies check it on boot.

tj: Proposed minimal activation sequence (unixy):

```
# assuming staged in /opt/redwood/staged-<id>
# record intent
echo "activating: <id>" > /var/lib/redwood/activation.marker
# atomic switch
mv /opt/redwood/current /opt/redwood/prev || true
mv /opt/redwood/staged-<id> /opt/redwood/current
# teardown previous after health checks
```

mira: Nice. Add a final atomic clear of activation.marker after successful health-checks, and a TTL to avoid stale markers blocking future activations.

devops: For offline delivery transport, we should support: 1) removable media (sneaker-net), 2) local rsync over an ephemeral mounting host, 3) air-gapped pull via jump-host. The manifest should include a transport_hint field so operator UI shows the right instructions.

shankar: For signature verification we must integrate with KMS or a local hardware key for high-security customers. But support a dev-mode with static key bundle for field testing.

leo: Rollback plan: we should precompute a revert-plan at stage time (list of files to restore, services to restart). Keep it as a small JSON alongside the manifest. Operator UI can run 'redwood rollback --apply-id <id> --fast' which runs the precomputed steps.

mira: How do we limit operator memory usage? If operator keeps only manifest + two small indices (blob digests + offsets) they can stream blobs to disk rather than caching. That makes staging slower but predictable.

tj: Also consider a double-buffer layout on disk: /opt/redwood/versions/<id>/ and symlink /opt/redwood/current -> versions/<id>. Rename of symlink is atomic on most filesystems when done with symlink swap (ln -sfn). That avoids moving large trees.

leo: Beware: ln -sfn is not universally atomic across NFS. For on-prem customers using distributed filesystems, we need a fallback: create a small activation token in the cluster metadata service and let the nodes pick the new version on next boot cycle.

sre-oncall: Observability: emit activation events with apply_id, bytes_staged, verify_latency, activation_duration, and final health_check_ok boolean. Also expose a small /metrics endpoint for rollout progress. Alerts: activation in-progress > 10m => page.

devops: We should provide a dry-run mode for operator that validates signatures and precomputes revert-plan without touching current symlink. UI shows estimated revert time and disk impact.

anya: Good callouts. One more: network-limited installs — allow chunked stream and resume. Keep chunk metadata in manifest so resume doesn't need global state.

tj: Example resume marker design:

```
# chunk manifest contains chunk_id, offset, size, sha256
echo "chunk:<id>:offset=<offset>" >> /var/lib/redwood/stage-progress-<apply_id>.log
# on resume, operator reads progress log and continues from last offset
```

shankar: Security: ensure all resume markers and progress logs are integrity protected (HMAC with the same key used for signature verification) to avoid tampering in a shared operator box.

mira: UX: operator console should expose 3 buttons: Stage, Activate, Rollback (fast). Each action shows required prechecks. Stage returns a small manifest summary and the precomputed rollback plan.

leo: Failure modes to document in the playbook: incomplete stage, activation marker present on boot, failed healthchecks, and partial service restarts. Provide manual steps for each with the exact commands to run to get to a known-good state.

anya: Action items:
- @tj to draft the activation script snippet and double-buffer layout README (eta: EOW)
- @mira to write small manifest schema addendum (includes transport_hint, revert_plan) (eta: 3 days)
- @shankar to attach signature verification streaming pseudo-code and KMS integration notes (eta: 3 days)
- @leo to draft playbook failure-mode checklist and systemd integration notes (eta: EOW)

ops-bot: deploy-checks: offline-pkg-lint passed (sha256: b4d9...) ; signature-schema lint passed. CI: 42/42 green.

devops: I'll mock an operator UI flow in a short screencast once docs land.

anya: OK — thanks all. If no blockers I'll fold this into an RFC follow-up and call out the new fields and scripts. :eyes:
